title: CNBC Technology Edge: IBM, DEC, and HP Adapting to Client-Server (Bruce Francis, with Tabak/Roach/Sochi/Kastner panel)
author: CNBC (host: Bruce Francis; panelists: George Tabak, Stephen Roach, Pat Sochi, Peter S. Kastner)
abstract: 29-minute CNBC Technology Edge episode hosted by Bruce Francis on the challenges facing IBM, Digital Equipment Corporation, and Hewlett-Packard as they transition from proprietary systems to open client-server architecture. Panelists: George Tabak (Ingersoll Rand), Stephen Roach (Morgan Stanley), Pat Sochi (Teleport Communications Group / TCG), and Peter Kastner (Aberdeen Group). Discussion covers customer-need responsiveness, integrated solutions, mainframe-to-client-server shift, industry consolidation potential, and the changing role of technology in business productivity. Panel consensus: HP most successful in transition, IBM recovering, DEC facing significant challenges. Source video archived in companion private repo shorttack/kastner-restricted-sources. importance_rationale: Captures a pivotal moment in the proprietary-to-open transition; Kastner appears as industry analyst alongside Stephen Roach and other major figures.

title: Informix Universal Server launch (December 1996): Object-Relational Database with DataBlades
author: Informix Software (Phil White, Mike Stonebraker, Ed Zander, Malcolm Colton, Dave Cope; with Peter S. Kastner)
abstract: 91-minute Informix Universal Server launch event. Phil White (CEO) introduces the product as a redefinition of database performance. Mike Stonebraker (CTO) presents object-relational databases as the next great wave in database technology, replacing traditional RDBMS. Ed Zander (Sun Microsystems) frames the alignment with network computing. Malcolm Colton (Director, Database Marketing) emphasizes ease of use, speed, extensibility. Dave Cope (GM, DataBlade Business Unit) introduces DataBlades — plug-in modules for image, video, spatial data. Partner DataBlade demos. White positions Informix as the most influential database for two consecutive years. Kastner appears as analyst providing time-to-market advantage commentary. title: Informix Competitive Update (1994-02-17): Kastner Briefs Informix Sales Force on Oracle/Sybase/Ingres RDBMS Market
author: Peter S. Kastner (Aberdeen Group, presenting to Informix sales team)
abstract: 42-minute Kastner presentation to Informix sales team, framing the RDBMS market as 'a jungle.' Covers Aberdeen's relational database buying guide; common playing-field features (architecture, ANSI SQL, referential integrity, stored procedures, triggers, two-phase commit); differentiating technologies (extensibility, scalability, dev tools, ease of use, performance, distributed access, large-DB support, standards); Informix strengths in scalability, 4GL dev tools, and performance; weaknesses in replication and large-DB support. Competitor profiles: Oracle, Sybase, Ask Ingres. Kastner introduced by Informix as 'a leading analyst in client-server, distributed data processing, OLTP, and the database industry' with background at Digital, Prime, Stratus, and ten years consulting with Arthur D. Little. Source video archived in companion private repo shorttack/kastner-restricted-sources. AI-generated summary transcript ingested 2026-06-12.
importance_rationale: Kastner is the sole presenter for a 42-minute session to Informix sales team — primary-source Aberdeen analysis of the early-1994 RDBMS competitive landscape.

title: CNBC: SARS Impact on Global Electronics Supply Chain (Kastner as Chief Research Officer, Aberdeen Group)

title: Software 2000 keynote: Kastner on the IT Paradigm Shift, Mainframe Evolution, and MIS Career Decisions
author: Software 2000 conference (featuring Peter S. Kastner, Aberdeen Group)
abstract: 7-minute Kastner keynote/segment at the Software 2000 conference on IT in the 1990s. Uses an early-rounds-of-a-prizefight metaphor for IT-project exhaustion. Outlines future MIS roles: security, corporate communications infrastructure, training. Closes on MIS career choice — technological infrastructure vs business-oriented competitive-advantage roles.
